replies.body: I tried the `new BatchScenario(this)` pattern here but it reads worse in Scala: the constructor has to take the Builder and manually copy each field, and the Builder fields need widening to `private[BatchScenario]` so the outer class can read them. The current direct-field constructor is more idiomatic for Scala, so I left it as-is. Happy to switch if you feel strongly.

replies.body:
Fixed in https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/commit/46cb449157d493ed901fec203f05dd6e885f0ad3.

Imported `java.lang.Long` as `JLong` and used it for both batchSize fields.

threads.body: `batchSize` returns `(long) size` for every size except `1`, so an empty transaction (size `0`) yields a batch size of `0L` instead of `null`. This is currently harmless because `DbClientAttributesExtractor` only emits `db.operation.batch.size` when the value is `> 1`, but returning `0` for an empty transaction is semantically misleading. Using `size > 1` expresses the intent directly and matches the condition used downstream.
